core1b.fresh_task: Two point sources are 30 cm apart on opposite sides of an ideal converging lens of f=12 cm. Their images are at the same finite global position. Find both source distances, identify which gives the real image, and verify the common global coordinate when the farther source is on the left.
core1b.protected_work: Translate two local lens axes to one laboratory axis, derive the shared-image constraint and reject degenerate solutions.

stages.predict: State the expected relationship or outcome and your uncertainty before solving.
stages.attempt: Two point sources are 30 cm apart on opposite sides of an ideal converging lens of f=12 cm. Their images are at the same finite global position. Find both source distances, identify which gives the real image, and verify the common global coordinate when the farther source is on the left.
stages.reconstruct: Let p+r=30. Equality of x_L=Fp/(p−F) and x_R=−Fr/(r−F) gives pr=FS/2=180. Roots z=(30±√180)/2≈21.708,8.292 cm. Farther p>12 forms real image x≈26.83 cm; nearer right r<12 gives local v≈−26.83 cm, global x≈+26.83 cm. Both coincide; reversing assignments flips global side.
stages.diagnose: Only if your saved answer exhibits this error: Using the same positive incident axis for both objects or accepting the double root at both focal points as a finite image. Otherwise record insufficient evidence.
stages.repair: Use local incident directions separately, convert v back to global x, and verify finite denominators and co-location.
stages.boundary_test: If both sources are on the same side of the lens, can two distinct finite object coordinates have one finite conjugate in the ideal thin-lens model?
